metadata.title: Identifying key factors of reading achievement: A machine learning approach

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PISA 2018 reading achievement data for students in four Chinese provinces/municipalities (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang), with an analytic sample of 12,058 students across 361 schools. The manuscript reports that PISA provides standardized Weighted Likelihood Estimates (WLE) and that the dependent variable is PV1READ, but it does not report applying any PISA sampling weights or replicate-weight procedures in the ML estimation. Because the models are tree-based (CART, Random Forest, RE-EM regression trees) and the paper does not mention weight-aware estimation, the analysis appears to be conducted without complex survey weighting. The main preprocessing steps described are school-grouped median imputation for missing values and a 70:30 random split into training and test sets.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used PISA 2018 reading assessment data restricted to four Chinese provinces/municipalities (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang), totaling 361 schools and 12,058 students. The dependent variable is PV1READ (PV1 as the outcome). Missing values were imputed using a school-based grouping strategy with median interpolation within each school group. After preprocessing, the dataset was randomly partitioned into training and test subsets using a 70:30 split.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (PV1READ), China (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang)
main_findings.performance_metrics: CART RMSE: 75.33; Random Forest RMSE: 62.89; RE-EM regression tree RMSE: 61.64; Integrated RE-EM regression tree (RE-EM RF) RMSE: 60.11 (best).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading (PV1READ) data for students in Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, and Zhejiang, the study leveraged Meta-cognition: assess credibility, Meta-cognition: summarizing, Joy/like reading, Science learning time, and Socioeconomic and cultural status to predict reading achievement, finding that the integrated RE-EM regression tree within a random forest framework achieved the lowest prediction error (RMSE = 60.11) and that Meta-cognition: assess credibility was the most influential feature. This indicates that strengthening students’ credibility-evaluation meta-cognition and reading enjoyment—especially for students below average—may be a high-leverage target for improving digital reading outcomes, though the study is predictive (not causal) and uses PV1READ with median imputation for missing values.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PISA 2018 digital reading achievement for 12,058 students in four Chinese provinces/municipalities (Beijing, Shanghai, Jiangsu, Zhejiang), using PV1READ as the dependent variable. It compares CART, Random Forest, RE-EM regression trees, and an integrated RE-EM regression tree embedded in a random forest framework, using a 70:30 train/test split and RMSE as the main performance metric. The integrated RE-EM RF model performs best with RMSE = 60.11 (vs. 75.33 for CART, 62.89 for RF, and 61.64 for RE-EM). Across models, Meta-cognition: assess credibility (METASPAM) is consistently the most important predictor, followed by Meta-cognition: summarizing (METASUM) and Joy/like reading (JOYREAD), with nonlinear effects including ceiling and S-shaped patterns. Limitations include the lack of reported complex-survey weighting in the ML estimation and the use of PV1READ rather than combining across all plausible values.
